definitions.gloss: one and only; unique; unparalleled; incomparable
definitions.explanation: Describes something or someone that is absolutely singular, with no equal or equivalent. A four-character compound emphasizing absolute uniqueness.

examples.japanese: {唯一無二|ゆいいつむに}の{存在|そんざい}だ。
{彼|かれ}の{才能|さいのう}は{唯一無二|ゆいいつむに}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: His talent is said to be unparalleled.

examples.japanese: この{寺|てら}は{世界|せかい}でも{唯一無二|ゆいいつむに}の{建築|けんちく}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: This temple is known as a truly unique piece of architecture in the world.

notes:
A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) composed of {唯一|ゆいいつ} (only one) + {無二|むに} (without a second). The two halves reinforce each other to emphasize absolute uniqueness — there is only one and no second exists.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {唯一無二|ゆいいつむに}の{存在|そんざい} (one-of-a-kind existence)
- {唯一無二|ゆいいつむに}の{才能|さいのう} (unparalleled talent)
- {唯一無二|ゆいいつむに}の{親友|しんゆう} (irreplaceable best friend)
- {唯一無二|ゆいいつむに}の{作品|さくひん} (unique work of art)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {唯一|ゆいいつ} — the only one; simpler and more common, without the emphatic reinforcement
- {独自|どくじ} — original, unique; focuses on being distinctive rather than being the sole one
- かけがえのない — irreplaceable; more emotional and personal in tone

USAGE:
This is a literary and emphatic expression. It is common in speeches, writing, and media when praising something as extraordinary. In everyday conversation, {唯一|ゆいいつ} alone is more common, while {唯一無二|ゆいいつむに} adds rhetorical weight.
